profile.title: Systems Changes
profile.canonical_definition: Public corpus for Systems Changes Learning: an action-learning programme on systems changes, living systems, temporality, contextual-dyadic thinking and practice.
profile.summary: A public research-and-learning corpus that develops a temporally sensitive account of systems changes in living systems.
profile.why_it_matters: It offers a contrasting grammar to stage-based change models and keeps doing, thinking and making together.
key_distinctions: changes rather than a singular planned change
rhythmic shifts rather than static states
common_misreadings: It is not simply another change-management sequence.
open_checks: Add comparative accounts from other living-systems and process traditions.
profile.editorial_note: Public account based on named sources; documentary provenance, interpretation and evaluative claims are kept distinct.

sources.notes: Primary account of Systems Changes Learning, including rhythmic shifts, texture/contexture, propensity, contextual-dyadic thinking and action learning.

sources.title: Knowing Better via Systems Thinking
sources.notes: Primary account that explicitly places contemporary systems approaches in longer systems-sciences traditions and uses that lineage as part of teaching systems thinking.

sources.notes: Primary record of Ing’s 2016 proposal to adapt generative pattern-language practice for service systems thinking, including the alternative pattern form of voices, values and spatio-temporal frames.
